
### exec*  {.smaller}


* exec* --- _replace_ current program with new program

   * `*`: multiple variants
   * same pid, new process image

* `int execv(const char *path, const char **argv)`

   * path: new program to run
   * argv: array of arguments, terminated by null pointer

* also other variants that take argv in different form and/or environment variables

   * []{.my-small} environment variables = list of key-value pairs


### execv example


```{.c code-line-numbers="true"}
...
child_pid = fork();
if (child_pid == 0) {
  /* child process */
  char *args[] = {"ls", "-l", NULL};
  execv(
     "/bin/ls",
     args
  );
  /* execv doesn't return when it works.
     So, if we got here, it failed. */
  perror("execv");
  exit(1);
} else if (child_pid > 0) {
  /* parent process */
  ...
}
```


### execv example


```{.c code-line-numbers="5,8"}
...
child_pid = fork();
if (child_pid == 0) {

  ...

```

::: {.myoverbox .my-small .midright}

*  second argument: used to compute new `argv`, `argc`
*  convention: first argument is program name
   *  can violate convention, supply whatever `argv[0]`

:::


### execv example


```{.c code-line-numbers="7"}
...
child_pid = fork();
if (child_pid == 0) {
  /* child process */
  char *args[] = {"ls", "-l", NULL};
  execv(
     "/bin/ls",
     args
  );
  /* execv doesn't return when it works.
     So, if we got here, it failed. */
  perror("execv");
  exit(1);
} else if (child_pid > 0) {
  /* parent process */
  ...
}
```

::: {.myoverbox .my-small .midright}

*  first argument: path of executable to run
*  on Unix, `/bin` is a directory <br/>with many common programs

:::
